title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
cScaleSummary: C0: all ingredients are plant-derived and contribute 0 mg dietary cholesterol per serving.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active because kidney beans provide a substantial legume component and dietary fiber. Light coconut milk limits, but does not eliminate, coconut saturated fat; cholesterol-free does not mean saturated-fat-free.
intro:
Jamaican rice and peas pairs fluffy rice with red kidney beans in a fragrant coconut broth. The peas in the name are beans, not green peas. Scallion, garlic, thyme, allspice, and a whole Scotch bonnet give the pot its characteristic flavor. Keeping the pepper intact provides aroma with gentler heat, though the heat varies and a split pepper makes the dish considerably hotter.

This version uses light coconut milk and a generous proportion of beans. Cook the beans fully before adding the rice, measure the cooking liquid, and give the covered pot a final rest. Serve as four substantial side portions alongside jerk chicken.

items.prep: for cooking the beans; extra water for soaking and keeping the beans submerged
measured after cooking; top up with water if needed
left whole and intact, including the stem

miseEnPlace: Sort and rinse {{ingredient:kidney-beans}}. Soak for 8-12 hours in plenty of water in the refrigerator, then drain and discard the soaking water.
Prepare {{ingredient:scallions}} and {{ingredient:garlic}} as specified. Wash {{ingredient:thyme}} and {{ingredient:scotch-bonnet}}; keep the pepper intact.
Rinse {{ingredient:rice}} until the water runs mostly clear and drain well.
Have a liquid measuring jug ready for {{ingredient:bean-liquid}} and a heavy saucepan with a tight-fitting lid ready for the rice.

stepGroups.title: Cook the Beans
items: Put the soaked and drained {{ingredient:kidney-beans}} in a saucepan with {{ingredient:bean-water}} and {{ingredient:bean-salt}}. Bring to a full rolling boil and boil for at least 30 minutes, adding hot water as needed to keep the beans submerged. Reduce to a simmer and continue cooking until fully tender with no firm or chalky center, usually another 30-60 minutes; older beans may take longer. Do not cook dried kidney beans solely in a slow cooker.

Drain the fully cooked beans into a bowl, saving the cooking liquid. Measure {{ingredient:bean-liquid}}, topping up with water if needed. Set the beans aside. Only the measured liquid goes into the rice pot.

stepGroups.title: Infuse the Coconut Broth
items: Combine {{ingredient:coconut-milk}}, the measured {{ingredient:bean-liquid}}, {{ingredient:rice-salt}}, {{ingredient:scallions}}, {{ingredient:garlic}}, {{ingredient:thyme}}, {{ingredient:allspice}}, and {{ingredient:black-pepper}} in a heavy saucepan. Gently add {{ingredient:scotch-bonnet}} without piercing it. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.

stepGroups.title: Cook the Rice
items: Add {{ingredient:rice}} and all the cooked beans. Stir gently once, keeping the pepper intact. Bring back to a gentle boil, cover tightly, and reduce the heat to its lowest setting. Cook for 18-20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed. Keep the lid closed and do not stir during cooking. If the rice is still firm and the pot is dry, add a small splash of boiling water, cover, and cook for another 3-5 minutes.

stepGroups.title: Rest and Serve
items: Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Carefully lift out the Scotch bonnet, thyme stems, scallion pieces, and garlic cloves. Fluff gently with a fork and serve with jerk chicken. For larger yields, use a wider heavy pot and judge doneness by the rice rather than multiplying the cooking time.
Refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours and use within 3-4 days. Reheat until steaming hot throughout with a splash of water.
